cases.prompt: Review the staged change described in the input file and give me your review with a merge recommendation. Do not run any commands; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: Uses the interactive report: a Review heading, a Verdict line, a Depth line with its reason, Blocking and Follow-up findings, Proofs, Claims checked
Verdict is changes-required because of the SQL injection and the never-matching usage increment
Findings cite file plus function, not line numbers
Names mutants the weak tests would let survive, marks unrun proofs as not run, and audits the 14-tests and expiry-covered claims against the log
Does not ask for new result types against the plain-dict convention

assertions.name: reviewer-quality
rubric: The f-string SQL in apply_discount is reported as a critical injection issue with a fix that uses the project's %s placeholder convention
The review notes that the UPDATE uses the un-normalised code, so lowercase input never increments uses, and that the cap check allows one use past max_uses
The review contrasts the author's 'All 14 tests pass' and 'expiry is fully covered' claims with the log showing 13 passed and the expiry test skipped
The review states which mutants (for example wrong discount math or a >= cap) the existing assertions would not catch, and proposes assertions that would

cases.prompt: An orchestrator agent has delegated the code review described in the input file to you. Write the report you would return to it. Do not run any commands; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: Returns the delegated report: a verdict line bound to head 3f9a2c1d, a Depth line, Blocking, Follow-up, Mutants, Claims checked, Not verified, Outside this PR, Long form
Verdict is changes-required or close: the helper swallows every timeout and the failed-jobs assertion was removed
Severity is rated on the findings, not lowered because this is round 3
The root cause and the 50-run and CI-green claims are marked unproven or refuted; the report has no markdown headings

assertions.name: reviewer-quality
rubric: The report identifies that waitForDrain swallows the final timeout, so the test passes even when the queue never drains, and rates it blocking
The removed expect(queue.failed) assertion is reported as lost coverage, and severity is not lowered because this is round 3
The '0 failures in 50 runs' claim and the CI run on main@b71e0a4 (before PR #409 touched src/retryQueue.ts) are marked unverified or refuted
The report does not claim any mutant or probe was actually run; unrun proofs appear under Not verified

cases.prompt: Review the pull request described in the input file and give me your review with a merge verdict. Do not run any commands; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: The review is sized by blast radius, not by the 'read-only, low risk' framing, because an external partner hard-codes the response next week
The verdict is changes-required, with the interface shape as a blocking finding despite green tests and full coverage
It names the costly shape: internal keys and table names in the URL and payload, internal status codes due to change, no version, a plain-text error, locale times, float dollars, unpaginated orders

assertions.name: reviewer-quality
rubric: The review rejects the 'low risk, tests green' framing and sizes the change by blast radius, because an external partner hard-codes the response next week
It names the costly-to-change shape: internal keys and table names in the URL and payload, single-letter status codes due to change, locale-formatted local times, dollars as floats, a plain-text 404
It proposes a contract to agree before merge: a versioned path, opaque IDs, documented enums with an unknown value, ISO-8601 UTC times, integer cents, a typed error body, paginated orders
It spends no findings on code style or test count, and does not take the teammate's LGTM as evidence

cases.prompt: Review my staged changes before I commit them.
Check this diff for bugs and tell me whether it is safe to merge.
The flaky-test fix is in; review it and prove the new test actually fails if the bug comes back.
Review this implementation plan before we start building and tell me what's missing.
expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: reviewing a plan before work starts belongs to plan-review

cases.prompt: Work through the Copilot review comments on my PR and fix the valid ones.
expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: working through review comments on your own PR is not reviewing a change

cases.prompt: Reply to the review threads on my PR and resolve the ones my last push fixed.
expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: replying to and resolving threads is not reviewing a change
